headline: Fog and sunny afternoons last through Thursday; a weak front Friday into Saturday brings light rain, cooler air, and possible frost.
summary: High pressure keeps western Washington mostly dry through Thursday. Expect fog and low cloud again overnight, most likely in the north interior from Bellingham to Everett, with low cloud and mist elsewhere. Thursday should have somewhat less cloud, so skies clear earlier and temperatures run slightly warmer, with sunny, seasonably warm afternoons. A weak front arrives late Friday into Saturday. Forecasters expect only a few hundredths of an inch of rain over the Cascades and northern Puget Sound, and it won't last long. The bigger change is cooler air, with Friday highs falling to the low 60s and breezy winds along the coast, the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and Puget Sound waterfront areas. Snow levels (the elevation where rain turns to snow) drop to around 5000 feet late Friday night, so higher terrain, especially the North Cascades, may get a dusting of snow. The weekend turns colder as low pressure settles over the Northwest. Saturday morning lows are forecast in the upper 30s at Cascade passes and the low 40s in the foothills, a few degrees cooler on Sunday morning. Forecasters say to stay tuned for possible frost or freeze concerns for crops and sensitive plants, but this is still being watched, not yet forecast. Cool weather should last into early next week. Another chance of rain comes Tuesday into Wednesday, but forecasters are less sure about it because the ensembles (groups of computer model runs) disagree on where the low-pressure area will end up. No watches, warnings, or advisories are in effect.
changes: The morning Dense Fog Advisory for Puget Sound and nearby waters expired at noon, and the evening update has no hazards. The timing of the Friday front shifted slightly to late Friday into Saturday, and the evening update focuses fog on the north interior.
